concepts.definition: An agent that perceives its environment through sensors and acts upon it via actuators to maximize an expected performance measure.
A framework for designing an agent, consisting of Performance measure, Environment, Actuators, and Sensors.
A characteristic of rational agents, where they operate under limited knowledge of their environment.
Protocols used in cooperative multi-agent systems to coordinate tasks without centralized bottlenecks.
Systems consisting of multiple agents that coordinate with each other to achieve a common goal.
